target_customer: Product and marketing teams (as Taplytics, mobile A/B testing), later software development teams (as DevCycle, feature flags)
problem: Teams could not test or change native mobile app experiences without shipping new app releases, and later could not release features gradually without flag tooling.
business_model: B2B SaaS, usage-based pricing for DevCycle rather than per seat
product_category: Mobile A/B testing, then feature flag management

founders.name: Aaron Glazer
founders.background_notes: BetaKit says the company was founded in 2011 by Aaron Glazer and TechCrunch 2015 names him CEO. He is not listed on the YC page, so the co-founder status rests on BetaKit.

founders.name: Jonathan Norris
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder and CTO on the YC page.

founders.name: Andrew Norris
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder and COO on the YC page; his bio mentions B2B sales, A/B testing, finance and operations.

founders.name: Cobi Druxerman
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder and CPO on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: A native mobile SDK that changed app elements at runtime without app store resubmission, which required careful iOS engineering in 2014, later extended to Android and analytics.

defensibility.rationale: SDK integration created some switching cost, but several competitors offered mobile testing and the category was open to free or bundled alternatives.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competitors in mobile testing existed from 2014, and the company later pivoted toward feature flags in 2022. Dynatrace bought the DevCycle platform in January 2026.

market_need_then: In March 2014 the company announced native iOS A/B testing for non-developers, and by late 2014 TechCrunch named customers Frank & Oak, WordPress and Homejoy, showing real early demand from mobile app teams.

branding.domain_note: Operates at devcycle.com; the original product was Taplytics at taplytics.com.

identity.logo: A logo with a playful 'Wink' variant per the site assets
identity.voice_and_tone: Conversational first person plural, focused on developer experience, per the 2023 brand origin post

rebrands.why: Moved from an A/B testing platform for marketing and product teams to a feature flag tool built for developers

brand_strength.rationale: Taplytics had YC and TechCrunch coverage, and DevCycle positioned around OpenFeature, but no sourced evidence of brand pull; the rebrand reset awareness.

pivots.from: Taplytics: A/B testing and experimentation for product and marketing teams
pivots.to: DevCycle: feature flag management for developers
pivots.why: Developer-focused feature management market; the company launched DevCycle as a new product in 2022

outcome_analysis: Taplytics began in 2011 as a mobile A/B testing tool, joined YC in Winter 2014 and raised a 2.4 million dollar seed from YC and well known angels. It survived a crowded testing market by launching DevCycle, a developer-focused feature flag product, in 2022, and reported 7.4 million dollars raised overall. Dynatrace bought the DevCycle platform in January 2026 for an undisclosed price, an exit consistent with a capital-light company that found a developer niche rather than a large venture outcome.
notes: The seed date is 2014 because the CEO said the round closed the previous summer, with the announcement on 2015-05-20. A Series A of 2.235 million led by Spider Capital appears in one trade snippet, and Wellfound lists a 7.8 million A round; these conflict and are unverified so no Series A is recorded. BetaKit gives total funding of 7.4 million. A snippet says DevCycle raised 5 million to scale the new product in 2022, not confirmed in an opened source. Founding year is conflicting (2011 on YC and BetaKit, 2013 or 2014 elsewhere). No dated competitor source near March 2014 was opened (Apptimize and Optimizely appear on undated comparison pages), so the list is empty. Founder education not found.
